subject: Termination and escrow options for SLA obligations - Helix Bio
messages:
From: Sylvia Kern <sylvia.kern@helixbio.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Thomas Nguyen <t.nguyen@helixbio.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 16:23:00 -0400
Subject: Helix request: termination rights and fee-at-risk for SLA breaches

Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement approval, legal and security are asking us to formalize stronger remedies than credits alone in the event of repeated platform unavailability or sustained latency regressions. For our regulated workflows we need clear operational levers.

Attached is our standard SLA rider (Helix_SLA_Request_202803.pdf) with the items we consider non-negotiable:
- Termination right (either party) after three separate P1 incidents in a 90-day window;
- Fee at risk equal to six months of committed spend held in escrow (or pre-funded) as liquidated damages for a sustained SLA failure window;
- A fixed per-incident LD amount for severity 1 incidents after cure period.

We understand Redwood's preference for credits, but Helix cannot accept credits alone for high-impact regulated workloads. We're prepared to offer a 24-month minimum committed term and introduce an executive escalation cadence in exchange for more robust exit and financial remedies.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can sign an escrow/loss-recovery clause and provide a redline to the proposed language? If not possible, please indicate the maximum capped cash exposure Redwood would accept.

Best,
Sylvia Kern
Head of Procurement
Helix Bio, Inc.

--- Attachment: Helix_SLA_Request_202803.pdf (PDF, 98KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Kern <sylvia.kern@helixbio.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helix request: termination rights and fee-at-risk for SLA breaches

Sylvia —

Thank you for the clear summary and the attached rider. I appreciate Helix's position and the desire for strong operational guarantees. A few quick points from our side:

- Redwood’s baseline SLA remedy is usage credits tied to verified downtime/latency windows and service credits that scale with severity.
- We are open to discussing limited cash exposure in specific enterprise cases, but Redwood has strict caps and cure periods to avoid perverse incentives.
- Termination for repeated P1s is something we can consider if a mutually agreeable escalation and remediation timetable is included (example: 30-day cure and progressive remediation plan).

I’m looping in Marissa from Legal and Ben from Solutions so they can review your proposed clauses and share a redline/counter. To keep momentum, would you be available for a 30-minute call on Thursday to walk through the proposed escrow mechanics and a proposed cap?

From Redwood’s POV, a couple of tradeoffs we’d propose up front: we can increase the escrow/cash exposure to up to three months’ committed fees (pre-funded escrow) if Helix accepts a 60-day cure window and a liability cap equal to 6 months of fees, with termination only after the cure window and certified third-party incident validation. That would be our starting point; Marissa will follow up with formal language.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

--- Attachment referenced: redwood_response_matrix.pdf (PDF, 42KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Helix request: termination rights and fee-at-risk for SLA breaches

Ben / Irene —

Forwarding Helix's rider. High-level legal position and proposed edits below (attached redline Helix_SLA_Redlines_v3.docx):

1) Escrow / fee-at-risk: Redwood is willing to consider a cash-based security up to the equivalent of three (3) months' committed fees, held in escrow with a neutral custodian. We will not accept an open-ended six-month pre-funded LD as proposed.

2) Termination: We can agree a termination right for repeated P1s only after:
   - A certified incident review that confirms coverage under the SLA;
   - A progressive remediation plan is provided and given a 30-60 day cure window (we recommend 60 days for complex infra fixes); and
   - No more than two independent P1s in any 90-day span before termination triggers. Helix's "three P1s" request is close, but we need the review/cure step baked in.

3) Per-incident LDs: We will not accept uncapped per-incident cash penalties. If Helix insists, propose a formula capped at the lesser of (i) 3 months' committed fees or (ii) a fixed dollar ceiling tied to the annual contract value.

4) Verification: Incidents must be validated by mutually agreed telemetry/monitoring (Redwood console logs + customer reported incidents) and, in disputed cases, a third-party SRR.

Next steps: I’ll attach a redline with our suggested language. Irene — please propose a call time. Ben — please prepare an ops note on how we would validate incidents and what telemetry we can share for the SRR.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

--- Attachment: Helix_SLA_Redlines_v3.docx (Word, 26KB)
From: Sylvia Kern <sylvia.kern@helixbio.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Thomas Nguyen <t.nguyen@helixbio.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 08:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Helix request: termination rights and fee-at-risk for SLA breaches

Irene / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick read. We appreciate Redwood being open to a pre-funded escrow, and the certification/verification steps make sense to Helix. A few clarifications from our side before the call:

- Helix would accept a 3-month escrow if the termination threshold remains at three P1s in 90 days rather than two. Reducing to two materially raises our downside risk because even intermittent cloud provider incidents can cascade into additional alerts.
- For per-incident LDs we prefer a straightforward schedule (e.g., $X per severity-1 incident after missed MTTR) rather than a percentage of committed fees. That helps our payout planning. If Redwood needs a cap, we can agree to three months' fees as an absolute cap.
- We are comfortable with the 60-day cure window for complex infra fixes, but Helix would like a guaranteed accelerated remediation path (weekly exec touchpoints) once we hit the second P1.

If Redwood can accept: (i) escrow = 3 months' committed fees, (ii) termination after 3 verified P1s in 90 days post-cure, and (iii) an LD schedule with a 3-month absolute cap, Helix will sign and attach a 24-month committed spend schedule to the contract in HubSpot deal HE-347. We can also execute a DocuSign NDA amendment to allow Redwood to share internal runbooks for joint incident reviews under a confidential binder.

Available for a call Thu 11:00–12:00 ET.

Best regards,
Sylvia Kern
Head of Procurement
Helix Bio, Inc.
